html:
The Sagas of Icelanders are prose stories written in Iceland in the 1200s and 1300s about the families who settled the island and their feuds in the 900s and 1000s.

Written in plain, spare Old Norse, they tell of killings, lawsuits, loyalty and revenge, often at the meetings of the Althing. Njáls saga, Egils saga and Laxdæla saga are among the best known. Their authors are mostly unknown, though Snorri Sturluson may have written Egils saga.

Together with the Eddas, the sagas preserve much of what is known of Norse myth, law and life, and the voyages to Greenland and Vinland, the Norse in America. They are among the treasures of medieval European literature, and Icelanders can still read them in the original. See Iceland and the settlement.
sum: The Sagas of Icelanders are prose stories written in Iceland in the 1200s and 1300s about the families who settled the island and their feuds in the 900s and 1000s.
